- No comprehensive nondiscrimination statute covering gender identity; protections only for government employees; recourse beyond federal complaint channels limited.
- First Pride with ~60 people — small community, tolerance at least minimally demonstrated.

Missing: parent national rules on documents/screening — not documented. This is an open question, not an exposure. Per rule 13, open questions are lighter.

Here, remedies are limited: no comprehensive nondiscrimination statute, recourse "beyond federal complaint channels is limited," hate-crime enhancement never documented as applied. Also unknown parent border regime for a document-mismatched traveller.

So: no documented adverse trans-specific incidents at all, plus positive legal signals (hate-crime law, marriage, no criminalisation), offset by absence of any working remedy and undocumented border/parent regime, and limited nondiscrimination coverage.

The 0.85 anchors all have documented working enforcement, which this lacks. The 0.75 anchors also have documented enforcement machinery. So I'd put this below 0.75. Something around 0.68–0.72. Given absent enforcement records and thin documentation plus unknown federal border practice and no functioning remedy, I lean ~0.68-0.70.
